fallbackMessage: I'm sorry, I don't have the answer to that. Here are some questions I can help with:
greeting: Hi! I'm Monica's portfolio assistant. Ask me anything below, or pick a suggested question.

intents.label: What year did Monica graduate?
examples: What year did I graduate?
When did Monica graduate?
What year did Monica graduate in?
intents.answer: I graduated from UC Berkeley in Fall 2024.

intents.label: Where did Monica go to school?
examples: What university did Monica attend?
Did she go to Berkeley?
Where did Monica study?
intents.answer: I attended UC Berkeley, where I earned degrees in Cognitive Science and Data Science, plus the Berkeley Certificate in Design Innovation.

intents.label: What did Monica study?
examples: What's her major?
What degrees does Monica have?
What did Monica major in?
intents.answer: I studied Cognitive Science and Data Science at UC Berkeley. I also earned the Berkeley Certificate in Design Innovation.

intents.label: Where is Monica based?
examples: Where does Monica live?
What city is she in?
Where is Monica located?
intents.answer: I'm based in Southern California.

intents.label: Is Monica open to relocation?
examples: Would Monica move for a job?
Is she open to relocating?
Can Monica relocate?
intents.answer: Yes, I'm open to relocation for full-time roles.

intents.label: What does Monica do?
examples: What's Monica's background?
Tell me about Monica
Who is Monica?
intents.answer: I'm Monica Cortes, a designer and data-minded creative passionate about using design and data for social good. My work has spanned nonprofits, university projects, and startups.

intents.label: What are Monica's skills?
examples: What is Monica good at?
What are her design skills?
Does Monica do UX research?
intents.answer: My skills include product design and UX research, visual and brand design, and strategy with data-informed design, from user research and prototyping to content strategy and marketing analytics.

intents.label: What kind of roles is Monica open to?
examples: What kind of roles are you open to?
What positions is Monica interested in?
What type of role is she seeking?
intents.answer:
I'm open to roles related to:
  • Design (visual or UX)
  • Marketing
  • Research
  • Data analysis
For the right role, I'm open to exploring something new.

intents.label: Is Monica open to freelance work?
examples: Are you available for freelance or contract work?
Does Monica do freelance?
Is Monica open to contract roles?
intents.answer: I'm primarily looking for full-time roles, but I'm open to hearing about freelance or contract opportunities if the scope and mission are the right fit.

intents.label: What tools does Monica use?
examples: What tools and software do you work with?
What design tools does Monica use?
What software is she proficient in?
intents.answer: I work in Figma for product and UX design, Adobe CC for publications and print, and Jira and Asana for collaboration. I'm also comfortable with data tools including Python and SQL, and I adapt to whatever stack a team already uses.

intents.label: What industries has Monica worked in?
examples: Do you have experience working in healthcare?
Has Monica worked in nonprofits?
Does she have tech industry experience?
intents.answer: My work spans nonprofits, higher education, and startup contexts. Examples include nenos (nonprofit), ScriptChain Health (health-tech), and UC Berkeley (higher education).

intents.label: What does Monica's design process look like?
examples: What does your design process typically look like?
How does Monica approach a new project?
What's her design workflow?
intents.answer: I adapt my process based on the team and project constraints. I try to gather as much context and research as possible upfront (stakeholder input, user needs, existing data), but if there isn't much to work with, I'll figure it out as I go. From there, I move into implementation and keep refining based on feedback and results.

intents.label: Is Monica open to remote work?
examples: Are you open to remote, hybrid, or in-person work?
Does Monica work remotely?
Is she open to hybrid roles?
intents.answer: I'm open to remote, hybrid, and in-person opportunities, and I'm willing to relocate for the right full-time role.

intents.label: When can Monica start?
examples: What's your availability?
When can you start?
How soon is Monica available?
intents.answer: I'm available for full-time opportunities now. For specific start dates, reach out at monicacortes@berkeley.edu.

intents.label: What kind of work is Monica looking for?
examples: Is Monica looking for work?
Is Monica available for full-time roles?
What opportunities is she pursuing?
intents.answer: I'm looking for full-time roles where I can use design and/or data for social good. I'm open to relocation for the right opportunity.

intents.label: What project is Monica most proud of?
examples: What's a project you're most proud of and why?
What's Monica's favorite project?
Which project means the most to her?
intents.answer: I'm proud of different projects for different reasons, whether I learned a new tool through the work or enjoyed the topic. If I had to choose one, my work and growth at UC Berkeley on the WSCUC report was especially meaningful. I felt like I was contributing to something bigger than myself at my own university.

intents.label: What is Monica learning right now?
examples: What's something you're learning right now?
What is Monica studying outside of work?
What skills is she building?
intents.answer: I'm developing myself as a better strategist who considers business and marketing, given my separate backgrounds in data science and visual design. Outside of work, I'm learning how to knit!

intents.label: What industry would Monica design for forever?
examples: If you could only design for one industry forever, what would it be?
What sector would Monica focus on indefinitely?
What mission area matters most to her?
intents.answer: I don't have a dream industry to work in, but I do prioritize work that feels like it's driving positive change or making people happy.

intents.label: Crochet or knitting?
examples: Crochet or knitting — which wins?
Does Monica prefer crochet or knitting?
Knitting vs crochet?
intents.answer: Crocheting is 100% easier, but I prefer knitting for clothes.

intents.label: How does Monica design for unfamiliar users?
examples: How do you approach designing for users you're not part of?
How does Monica design for people unlike her?
How does she build empathy with users?
intents.answer: I start with research: interviews, observation, and understanding constraints, rather than assuming I already know the answer. I test early, listen closely in usability sessions, and treat users as experts on their own experience.

intents.label: How do data science and design overlap for Monica?
examples: What's the overlap between your data science and design work?
How does Monica combine data and design?
How do her data and design skills work together?
intents.answer: In practice, I use data to frame problems, track performance, and validate design decisions, not just to make something look pretty. On projects like ScriptChain Health, research and analytics informed clearer creative direction and strategy.

intents.label: Has a project changed how Monica thinks about design?
examples: Have you worked on a project that changed how you think about design?
What project shifted Monica's perspective?
Did any work change her design philosophy?
intents.answer: Unlocked Labs deepened my appreciation for designing within real constraints, balancing user needs, stakeholder goals, and what a small team can actually ship.

examples: What kind of team culture do you do your best work in?

What kind of team does she prefer?
intents.answer: I do my best work on collaborative, cross-functional teams where designers talk regularly with engineers, researchers, and non-technical stakeholders, and where feedback is direct but constructive.

intents.answer: Yes, I've created social and marketing content for startups and organizations. See my most notable work for ScriptChain Health.

intents.answer: Yes, I have experience with marketing analytics and reporting, using data to understand what's working and adjust creative direction accordingly.

examples: Have you designed marketing collateral from scratch?
Has Monica designed ads, emails, or landing pages?
Does she create marketing materials?
intents.answer: Yes, I've designed marketing collateral from scratch, including social posts, print materials, reports, and digital assets for startups and UC Berkeley.

intents.label: How does Monica design for existing brands?
examples: How do you approach designing for a brand you didn't build?
How does Monica work within an existing brand?
Can she design for someone else's brand system?
intents.answer: Monica starts by learning the brand's existing rules, voice, and constraints — then extends the system thoughtfully rather than reinventing it. She's done this for university, nonprofit, and startup clients with established identities.

intents.label: How does Monica balance aesthetics and usability?
examples: How do you balance aesthetics with usability?
Does Monica prioritize beauty or usability?
How does she make designs both pretty and usable?
intents.answer: I treat aesthetics and usability as partners, not opposites. Visual clarity should help people understand and navigate a product. I test whether beautiful choices still work for real users before calling something done.

examples: What's a design trend you're skeptical of right now?
What design trends does Monica question?
Is there a trend she avoids?
intents.answer: I'm skeptical of trends that prioritize visual novelty over clarity, especially when they make interfaces harder to use or exclude people. If a trend doesn't serve the user, I'm not interested.

intents.label: What data tools does Monica use?
examples: What tools do you use for data analysis?
Does Monica use SQL or Python?
What data analysis software does she know?
intents.answer: Most of my work has been done through Python and SQL. I'm also comfortable building visualizations and synthesizing findings into design or strategy recommendations, and I adapt tooling to whatever a project requires.

intents.label: Has Monica turned data into design decisions?
examples: Have you turned a data finding into a concrete design or strategy decision?
How has Monica used data to change a design?
Does she act on analytics findings?
intents.answer: Yes, on strategy and marketing work, I've used performance data and research findings to refine messaging, layout priorities, and content direction rather than treating analytics as a separate step.

intents.label: What makes a good data visualization?
examples: What does a good data visualization look like to you?
How does Monica approach data viz?
What makes charts effective?
intents.answer: A good visualization answers one clear question fast, with honest scales, readable labels, and enough context that a non-technical viewer knows what to do next.

intents.label: Has Monica worked with messy data?
examples: Have you worked with messy or incomplete datasets?
Does Monica clean data?
How does she handle incomplete data?
intents.answer: Yes, my Data Science background includes working with incomplete or messy datasets, cleaning and synthesizing what's available before drawing conclusions or making recommendations.

intents.label: Has Monica worked with engineers?
examples: Have you worked directly with engineers or developers on a product?
Does Monica collaborate with dev teams?
Has she partnered with engineers?
intents.answer: Yes, I've collaborated closely with engineers and developers on product work, including handoff, feasibility conversations, and iterating within technical constraints.

intents.label: How do you handle multiple project deadlines?
examples: How do you handle deadlines across multiple projects?
How do you prioritize when you have multiple projects?
How do you manage multiple project deadlines?
intents.answer: I work on multiple projects depending on the deadline itself, but I also don't burn myself out by forcing myself to focus on only one. I tend to work wherever I feel most motivated, and sometimes get ahead on something if I foresee upcoming deadlines becoming a problem.

intents.label: Has Monica done user research?
examples: Have you conducted user interviews or usability tests?
Does Monica run usability sessions?
What has she learned from user research?
intents.answer: Yes, I've conducted user interviews and usability testing across product projects. I've found that early, lightweight sessions often surface assumptions worth fixing before too much gets built.

intents.label: How does Monica explain design to stakeholders?
examples: How do you communicate design or data decisions to non-technical stakeholders?
How does Monica present work to executives?
Can she explain design to non-designers?
intents.answer: I tie recommendations to goals stakeholders already care about, using plain language, visuals, and evidence from research or data rather than design jargon.

intents.answer: You can reach me at monicacortes@berkeley.edu, or connect with me on LinkedIn.

intents.answer: Outside of work, I enjoy media commentary, crocheting, Formula 1, and watching rom-com and thriller movies. I'm also building my full-stack skills for personal and professional projects.
